fields.h1: Build a Donation Request Form That Sorts Every Ask
fields.hero_description: Build a donation request form that takes asks from schools and charities and checks each one against your giving policy.
fields.features_heading: What a Business Checks Before It Gives
fields.features_subheading: Every group asks in its own way. Emergent builds the form and the giving log that sort each request before a manager reads it.
fields.feature_1:
Policy questions come before the ask

Ask for the event date, the group's EIN, and its exemption letter before the request itself. The app checks the date against your lead time and files the letter with the request.
fields.feature_2:
Each ask checked against the year's budget

Set one giving budget for the year. Every request shows the amount already committed and what would be left after a yes. The approver sees that balance before deciding.
fields.feature_3:
Requests routed by store and by amount

Send each request to the manager of the store the group picks. Anything above that store's limit goes to a regional manager by email, with the full request and its letter attached.
fields.feature_4:
Cash, gift cards or products, asked apart

Let each group choose cash, a gift card, products, or a sponsorship. Each type asks its own questions, such as logo placement for a team sponsor or retail value for a raffle prize.
fields.feature_5:
A decision email the group can act on

Approve or decline on the request page. The app writes back to the group with the decision, plus pickup details for a gift card or the date the check goes in the mail to them.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase, exported on paid plans

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans when giving requests need to sit next to your other systems. Host it where you like and keep building on top of it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Businesses, Four Kinds of Ask
fields.tab_content_1:
Gift card asks need 30 days or more, and this one gave 51

School auctions ask Oxbow Tavern for gift cards. The Sedgewick Elementary PTA wants a $50 card for its Mar 14 auction, 51 days out. The tavern turns down any ask under 30 days. This one clears that line, with the PTA's EIN and exemption letter attached. Owner Dario Pellandini gets an email that a request is in.
fields.tab_content_2:
After $750 for jerseys, $900 is left

Brackett Brewing sets aside $6,000 a year for team sponsorships, and $4,350 is already committed. Eastside Under-12 Soccer asks for $750 toward jerseys with the brewery's logo on the sleeve. Marketing lead Wren Hatchett opens it from a Slack alert and sees $900 would be left for the year after a yes.
fields.tab_content_3:
By store and by amount, a $400 ask reaches Marcus

Hollis Hardware runs 6 stores, and each store manager can approve up to $250. The Fairhaven Little League picks Store 4 on the form and asks for $400 in field supplies. Anything over the $250 limit goes to regional manager Marcus Trell. He gets the email, and the Store 4 manager is copied.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which three groups have not sent a photo?

Kestrel Bakery approved 9 donations this quarter and wants to know what each one did. The app emails every group 14 days after its event to ask what the event raised and for one photo. Six groups have answered. Owner Beatriz Coulter-Ames sees the 3 still waiting on one list and sends each a second email from it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Donation Request Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a donation request form that applies your giving policy to every ask, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the giving policy first
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the event date before the ask
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Split the form by what is asked for
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what you give and how much each year before you write a single question. A restaurant might give gift cards to schools only. A brewery might fund youth teams up to a set yearly amount. The form follows whatever you write here.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the event date near the top of the form. A lead-time rule needs that date to work, and a group that is too late hears it before filling in the rest. Pick a number of days you can turn a request around in.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the group's EIN and a copy of its IRS exemption letter, and make the upload required before the form can be sent. The letter then sits with the request, and whoever approves it reads both on one screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give cash, gift cards, products, and sponsorships their own branch of questions. A raffle prize needs a retail value and a pickup date. A sponsorship needs logo placement and the team's season dates. Keep each branch to a handful of questions.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the budget and who decides
fields.howto_step_5_des: Enter the year's giving budget and the dollar limit each person can approve alone. Requests above a limit go to the next person up. Write each limit as a number, such as $250 for a store manager, and name the person above it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put every rule from the last four steps into one prompt, along with the follow-up you want after each event. Emergent writes the request database and the email and Slack alerts from it. Change any rule later by describing the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one ask for an event 10 days away and one for an event 60 days away. The first should get the decline email and the second should reach the owner. Then submit an ask over your top limit and check who gets it.

faq_plan.q: What is a donation request form?
faq_plan.a: A donation request form is the form a business or foundation puts on its site so community groups can ask it for cash, products, or a sponsorship. It keeps the event and the group's details with the ask, ready to check against the business's own policy.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a donation request form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: what you give and the rules each request has to pass. Emergent builds the form and a database that holds every request. Publish it on your site and change any rule with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should a donation request form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the group's contact person and EIN, plus its exemption letter. Then ask what the event is and when, followed by the item requested and its dollar value. Add a field for how the business would be recognized. An Emergent form has no cap on how many requests it collects.

faq_plan.q: Is a donation request form for giving money or for asking for it?
faq_plan.a: It is for asking. A donation request form lets a group ask a business for a gift, while a donation form collects gifts from donors. The business reviews each request, then approves or declines it, and the group hears back either way.

faq_plan.q: What lead time should a donation request form require?
faq_plan.a: Choose a lead time you can meet and state it at the top of the form. Thirty days leaves room to review a request and get a gift card or product ready before the event. Put the event date first and send a short, polite decline for anything sooner.

faq_plan.q: Should a donation request form ask for proof of tax-exempt status?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the giving policy covers only tax-exempt groups. Request the group's EIN along with the IRS exemption letter, which states the Code section. The IRS also runs a Tax Exempt Organization Search, and notes that it provides a partial listing of recognized organizations. Keep the letter on file with the request either way.

faq_plan.q: Can a donation request form send requests to different approvers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Route each request by store or by amount: asks up to a store's limit go to its manager, and larger ones go to a regional manager. Approval by amount works the same way on a training request form. Every decision is saved in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How does a donation request form stay within a yearly giving budget?
faq_plan.a: It checks each request against a running total. Set the year's budget once, and the app adds every approved amount to what is already committed. Each new request shows the balance a yes would leave. If the budget changes mid-year, describe the new total to Emergent and it changes the rule.

faq_plan.q: What should a donation request form send when a request is declined?
faq_plan.a: It should send a short email that thanks the group and says plainly that the business cannot give this time. If a policy decided it, such as an event inside the lead time, name the policy. Close with the date your next budget year opens, and keep the whole email to a few sentences.

faq_plan.q: Can a donation request form follow up after the event?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Have the app email each group a set number of days after its event, asking for the total raised and one photo. Track who has answered on one list and resend from there. The same timed follow-up works on a maintenance request form, asking whether a repair held.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable PDF forms from single businesses and foundations, a WPForms template a business puts on its site so nonprofits can ask it for a donation, and how-to-ask articles (Springly, an in-kind letter guide). Every result is the blank sheet; none shows what a business does with forty requests a season. This page is for the business or company that receives donation and sponsorship requests from schools, teams and charities: a form that asks for the event date, the ask and the group's EIN and exemption letter, holds a lead-time rule, checks each ask against the year's giving budget, routes each store's requests to its manager, and follows up after the event. Donors giving money stay on the donation form page and gift receipts on the donation receipt page.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Donation Request Form That Sorts Every Ask', meta title 'Donation Request Form Builder for Businesses | Emergent' and hero 'Build a donation request form that takes asks from schools and charities and checks each one against your giving policy.' state the whole job; how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Business-side builder page: FAQ 1 defines the form, FAQ 3 lists what it should include, FAQ 4 separates it from a donation form, seven-step how-to, comparison table; meta promises (lead time, budget, routing, follow-up) are each delivered in tabs 1-4.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'The Sedgewick Elementary PTA wants a $50 card for its Mar 14 auction, 51 days out', 'each store manager can approve up to $250', 'logo placement for a team sponsor or retail value for a raffle prize'.

openers.evidence: Every feature body opens on a verb ('Ask for', 'Set one giving budget', 'Send each request', 'Let each group', 'Approve or decline', 'Export'); tab paragraphs open on full sentences ('School auctions ask Oxbow Tavern for gift cards.').

craft.evidence: Varied sentence lengths, one idea each; notes only (serial-comma inconsistency, a tacked-on 'to them' in feature 5).

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and concrete detail ('Owner Dario Pellandini gets an email that a request is in', 'Six groups have answered'); no AI-tell vocabulary or hype.

truth.evidence: Every number agrees across fields: 30 days (tab 1, chip add, mockup, image rule, FAQ 5 'Thirty days'), $6,000-$4,350-$750=$900 (tab 2, mockup, image kv), $250 limit (tab 3, how-to 05, image), 14 days and 6 of 9 (tab 4, mockup, image). FAQ 6 IRS statements match their irs.gov spans ('exemption letter, which states the Code section'; 'provides a partial listing'); no deductibility or tax advice. Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, no-caps, code-export; free-start appears on the share image ('Free to start').

distinct.evidence: Business receiving asks, not a donor-facing donation form (/donation) or a receipt (/donation-receipt); FAQ 4 'A donation request form lets a group ask a business for a gift, while a donation form collects gifts from donors.'

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in the first sentence ('It is for asking.', 'Yes, if the giving policy covers only tax-exempt groups.'); hub link in item 2; sibling links to donation, training-request, maintenance-request; no brands or file formats in questions.
